citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv.
creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
description: AMASS is a large unified human motion capture dataset that combines 15 optical marker-based mocap datasets into a common representation using SMPL body shape, pose, and DMPL soft-tissue parameters. It contains 42 hours of motion data from 346 subjects and 11,451 motions, providing fully rigged 3D human meshes and motion parameters for research.
name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper evaluates the quality of the fitted representations using the SSM dataset with synchronized 4D scans and mocap, reporting scan-to-model distance metrics for shape, pose, and soft-tissue reconstruction accuracy. The authors also manually inspected AMASS results and corrected or excluded problematic sequences.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels are not crowdsourced annotations; instead, the dataset parameters were produced by fitting MoSh++ to marker-based mocap data to recover SMPL body shape, pose, hand pose when markers are present, and soft-tissue dynamics. The outputs were then manually inspected, with errors corrected or problematic data held out.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that existing source mocap datasets are often narrowly focused on particular classes of motions and vary across laboratory-specific procedures and marker sets; AMASS is designed to mitigate these representation biases by unifying diverse datasets without normalizing all bodies to a common skeleton.
rai:dataCollection: AMASS was created by downloading publicly available motion capture datasets from the internet, obtaining several datasets privately, and recording some datasets by the authors. The authors then used MoSh++ to map marker-based optical mocap recordings from 15 source datasets into a common SMPL representation.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper notes inherent mocap problems such as marker occlusion, swapped and mislabeled markers. When markers are missing due to occlusion, MoSh++ increases the pose prior weight based on the number of missing markers, and problematic results were manually corrected or held out.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source data are optical marker-based human motion capture recordings from 15 datasets, with varying marker sets ranging from 37 to 91 markers placed at different locations on the body.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes limitations including inherent mocap issues such as swapped, mislabeled, missing, and occluded markers. Hand articulation is only captured when hand markers are present, and the authors note future work to extend captures to articulated hands and facial mocap markers.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-collection, the source mocap marker data were transformed using MoSh++ into a unified SMPL/DMPL parameterization with body shape, pose, hand articulation when available, and soft-tissue dynamics. The method also uses marker-count scaling and missing-marker weighting during fitting.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors used MoSh++ to convert the source marker trajectories into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters in a common format. Because mocap data can contain swapped and mislabeled markers, they manually inspected the results and either corrected problems or held out problematic sequences.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that they will continue to expand the dataset, continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by themselves and the community, and support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for machine learning applications in animation and computer vision, and is described as useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++, SMPL, SMPL-H, DMPL, and MANO were used to automatically fit and generate body shape, pose, hand articulation, and soft-tissue parameters from marker-based mocap data.
